prompt: Which of these changes creates a new revision of a Cloud Run service?
hint: Is it part of the template?

choices.text: Moving 10% of traffic to another revision
choices.why: Traffic belongs to the service, not to a revision.

choices.text: Adding a tag to an existing revision
choices.why: A tag is an entry in the traffic list.

choices.text: Changing an environment variable
choices.why: Right. Anything in the template makes a new revision.

choices.text: Reading the service's logs in Cloud Logging
choices.why: Reading changes nothing.

prompt: Why is a rollback on Cloud Run safer than a redeployment of yesterday's code?

choices.text: Only traffic moves
choices.why: Right. No build, no new image, nothing that can fail differently.

choices.text: A rollback skips the health checks
choices.why: Nothing is skipped; nothing new is built.

choices.text: Old revisions run on faster machines
choices.why: Revisions do not choose machines.

choices.text: Cloud Run caches yesterday's responses
choices.why: There is no response cache involved.

prompt: With --revision-suffix=v2, the service orders gets a revision named orders-___.
hint: The suffix follows the service name.

prompt: At home, orders-v2 answered in about a quarter of a second and orders-v1 in a few milliseconds. What caused the difference?

choices.text: orders-v2 was built from a newer image
choices.why: Both ran orders:1.

choices.text: Port 8082 is slower than port 8081
choices.why: Ports have no speed.

choices.text: K_REVISION makes the program log more
choices.why: It only changes the name in the answer.

choices.text: ORDERS_DELAY_MS=250 in orders-v2
choices.why: Right. A change of configuration, which is a new revision.

prompt: In the capture, how many seconds did orders-v2 take to answer /orders? Answer to two decimals.
What does a Cloud Run service's address point at?

choices.text: The newest revision, always
choices.why: Only while the split says LATEST at 100%.

choices.text: A traffic split
choices.why: Right. By default, LATEST at 100%.

choices.text: A fixed instance chosen at deployment
choices.why: Instances come and go.

choices.text: The revision with the most instances
choices.why: Instance counts follow the split, not the reverse.

prompt: With 90% to orders-v1 and 10% to orders-v2, a user loads three pages. What can they see?

choices.text: Only one version, chosen when they first arrive
choices.why: Nothing keeps a user on one revision.

choices.text: Only orders-v1, until 10% of all users have arrived
choices.why: The split is per request, not per user count.

choices.text: Both versions, since each request is assigned on its own
choices.why: Right. Consistency per user needs a flag in the application.

choices.text: orders-v2 on every tenth page exactly
choices.why: Assignment is random in proportion, not a rotation.

prompt: The plan accepted traffic blocks of 90% and 20%. What happens at apply?

choices.text: Cloud Run's API refuses it with an error
choices.why: Right. The sum is checked on Google's side.

choices.text: Cloud Run scales both to fit 100%
choices.why: Nothing rescales; the request is refused.

choices.text: The extra 10% goes to LATEST
choices.why: There is no overflow rule.

choices.text: Terraform rejects it before calling Google
choices.why: The plan showed it does not check the sum.

prompt: A split has LATEST at 10% and orders-v1 at 90%. A developer deploys a quick experiment. Who receives 10% of users?

choices.text: orders-v2, because LATEST was pinned when it was set
choices.why: LATEST is not pinned; it follows the newest.

choices.text: Nobody, until the split is updated
choices.why: LATEST's share moves without an update.

choices.text: orders-v1, which takes over LATEST's share
choices.why: Named revisions keep their own share only.

choices.text: The experiment, because it is now the latest revision
choices.why: Right. That is why mixing LATEST with named revisions is confusing.

prompt: Match each traffic entry to what it does.

pairs.right: An address with no share of traffic

right_distractors: Deletes the revision after a day

prompt: What does a tag give a revision?

choices.text: A share of the service's traffic
choices.why: A tag can have 0%; the share is the percent.

choices.text: An address of its own
choices.why: Right. canary---orders-….run.app.

choices.text: Protection from being deleted
choices.why: Tags do not protect anything.

choices.text: A guarantee of one warm instance
choices.why: That is a minimum number of instances.

prompt: A team used --no-traffic once for a careful release, then deployed three fixes the normal way. Users see none of them. Why?

choices.text: The fixes failed their startup probe
choices.why: Nothing says they failed; they received no traffic.

choices.text: Cloud Run waits a day before routing to a new revision
choices.why: There is no such wait.

choices.text: Nothing points at LATEST any more, until --to-latest
choices.why: Right. Later deployments take no traffic either.

choices.text: The tag kept all traffic on the first revision
choices.why: A tag reaches a revision; it does not hold the split.

prompt: Why remove the canary tag when the rollout is over?

choices.text: It stays public and guessable
choices.why: Right. Removing the tag removes the address.

choices.text: Tags are billed by the hour
choices.why: Tags cost nothing in themselves.

choices.text: A tag blocks deleting old revisions
choices.why: That is not why; the address is the risk.

choices.text: Tags expire anyway after a rollout
choices.why: They stay until removed.

prompt: Put the usual sequence for a careful release in order.
items: Give the revision a small percentage
Move to 100% and remove the tag
trap: A percentage before the tests sends real users to code nobody has tried.

prompt: A service takes 2,000 requests an hour and the canary has 10%. How many hours until it has seen 10,000 requests?
Which command, from gcloud's own examples, rolls everything back to the old revision?

choices.text: gcloud run services update-traffic myservice --to-latest
choices.why: That sends everything to the newest one.

choices.text: gcloud run deploy myservice --no-traffic
choices.why: That creates a revision; it moves nothing back.

choices.text: gcloud run services delete myservice
choices.why: That removes the service and every revision.

choices.text: update-traffic with --to-revisions=OLD=100
choices.why: Right. A rollback is a change of traffic.

prompt: A rollout rolled back to orders-v1 and orders-v1 now fails on every request. The image did not change. What is the likely cause?

choices.text: Old revisions decay after a week
choices.why: A revision is immutable.

choices.text: The new code changed the data, and the old code cannot read it
choices.why: Right. The code went back and the data did not.

choices.text: Cloud Run deleted orders-v1's image to save space
choices.why: Revisions keep their images by digest.

choices.text: The tag canary still points at orders-v2
choices.why: A tag affects only its own address.

prompt: What should be written down before a rollout starts? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The metric to watch for each revision
choices.why: Right; latency and errors, per revision.

choices.text: The threshold that triggers a rollback
choices.why: Right; decided before anyone is tempted to wait.

choices.text: The run.app address of the new revision
choices.why: It is assigned by Google and not a decision.

choices.text: How long each stage lasts
choices.why: Right; a stage of very little traffic sees very little.

prompt: Google Cloud ___ automates canary stages for Cloud Run, moving traffic by pipeline.
Order the moves in gcloud's update-traffic examples as one rollout that fails.
trap: The last move is a rollback, and it builds nothing.

prompt: Which belongs to a revision rather than to the service?

choices.text: The traffic split between revisions
choices.why: The split is the service's.

choices.text: The service's run.app address
choices.why: The address is the service's.

choices.text: Memory and environment variables
choices.why: Right. They are in the template.

choices.text: The list of tags
choices.why: Tags are entries in the service's traffic list.

prompt: A checkout redesign must look the same to a user across every page they open during the rollout. What does the lesson suggest?

choices.text: A flag in the application that decides per user
choices.why: Right. The split cannot keep a user on one revision.

choices.text: A 50% split, so each user sees it half the time
choices.why: Half the time is exactly the inconsistency to avoid.

choices.text: A tag, sent to every user by email
choices.why: That makes the tag public and skips the rollout.

choices.text: LATEST at 10%, which sticks per user
choices.why: LATEST is not sticky either.

prompt: At 50% of 2,000 requests an hour, how many hours to expect ten occurrences of an error that happens once in a thousand requests?
A deployment that should receive no requests at all uses the flag --no-___.
What does K_REVISION hold inside a Cloud Run container?

choices.text: The image's digest, as Artifact Registry lists it
choices.why: The digest is not passed as a variable here.

choices.text: The percentage of traffic it receives
choices.why: The container is not told its share.

choices.text: The tag of the address that was called
choices.why: Tags are not passed to the container.

choices.text: The name of the revision serving the request
choices.why: Right. orders-v1 or orders-v2 at home.
